tools.description: The printer's tool tree: its heads and the feeder slots on them, keyed by ids such as 0 and 0.2. It is read out of the state tree, so a printer that is away answers with what it said last. Absent on a printer that has said nothing about its tools.

unit_uid.description: What the printer calls itself on its connector's wire, empty for a connector whose devices have no such identifier. It is not this server's id, which is minted here, and it is not the serial number, which some firmware does not send. A printer that reported no serial is rendered with this value as its serial as well.

verbs.description: Every verb of this printer's kind this caller may send, sorted. The credential's scope narrows it as it narrows actions. A dangerous verb such as core.command.flash is here only when a grant or ownership of the printer gives it to the caller. A verb in capabilities and missing here is a command the server refuses this caller.

default.description: What the host sends when a command leaves it out. Absent when there is none.

enum.description: The only values accepted. Absent when any value of the type is accepted.

key.description: The capability key of this argument: the verb, a hash sign and the name.

max_length.description: The longest value accepted, in bytes, for a string. Absent when there is no bound.

maximum.description: The highest value accepted, inclusive, for a number. Absent when there is no upper bound.

minimum.description: The lowest value accepted, inclusive, for a number. Absent when there is no lower bound.

name.description: The name a command carries the value under, in args.

required.description: Whether a command must carry it.

type.description: How the value is read. Every value travels as text in args; this is what that text must parse as.

unit.description: What a number counts in. Absent for a value with no unit, such as a count or an index.

x_mm.description: The width of the area a print may cover, in millimetres.

y_mm.description: The depth of the area a print may cover, in millimetres.

z_mm.description: The highest a print may reach, in millimetres.

capabilities.description: Every verb and feature the device has, sorted by key. Empty for a device whose session has ended.

capability_epoch.description: The epoch the device record carries. A set read under an older epoch describes a session that has ended.

device_id.description: The device these capabilities belong to.

profile_matched.description: Whether a capability profile covered this model and firmware. False means the driver baseline is in force.

arguments.description: Every argument the verb accepts, sorted by name. Empty for a verb that takes none and for a feature.

key.description: The capability key, as the device record lists it and a command names it under verb.

at.description: When the session ended, as this server saw it.

reason.description: Why the session ended. session_ended is the connector releasing the printer, which covers every way a machine stops answering. server_stopping is this server shutting down, so the printer is not known to have gone anywhere.

base_model.description: The family of the feeder's model, such as MMU3.

mmu_command_in_progress.description: The command the multi-material unit runs now, as one character, such as L for a load, U for an unload and T for a toolchange. Absent while it runs none.

mmu_progress_code.description: The progress code the multi-material unit reports: the step of its work it is at, 0 when it is done. The codes are the multi-material unit firmware's.

model.description: The feeder's model, such as MMU3.

slot_count.description: How many slots the feeder has, enabled or not. Its slots are the child ids 0 to slot_count - 1.

type.description: The kind of feeder. The architecture allows only MMU now.

display_name.description: The name written for a person, absent when the printer reports only one name.

estimated_seconds.description: The print time the slicer estimated, in whole seconds, as the printer read it out of the file. It is present only on the directory of an answer about one print file, and absent for a printer or a file that names none.

folder.description: Whether the entry holds other entries.

layer_height_mm.description: The layer height the file was sliced with, in millimetres. Present only on the directory of an answer about one print file that names it.

material.description: The material the file was sliced for, one for each tool joined by a semicolon, such as PLA;PETG. Present only on the directory of an answer about one print file that names it.

modified.description: When the entry last changed, as an RFC 3339 string. The printer reports whole seconds, so this value has no fraction of a second. It is absent for a board that reported no timestamp.

name.description: What the printer addresses the entry by. On a FAT storage that is the short name, which is not what a person reads.

path.description: The storage-prefixed path, such as usb/models/part.bgcode. It is what the files endpoint takes.

printer_model.description: The printer the file was sliced for, such as XL2IS. Present only on the directory of an answer about one print file that names it.

read_only.description: Whether the printer refuses to change this entry.

size.description: Bytes the entry occupies, zero for a folder.

kind.description: multi takes a comma-separated list of values; text takes one string.

max_length.description: For text: the longest value the server accepts.

param.description: The query parameter this filter is sent as.

values.description: For multi: the values present among the printers this caller may see, and every value the request selected.

count.description: How many printers choosing this value would list, with every other filter applied and this filter's own selection ignored. For tag the selection stays applied, because tags narrow by AND: the printers carrying every chosen tag and this one.

value.description: One value the caller may filter by, spelled as the first device carrying it spells it.

detail.description: What the machine itself said, in its own words, when the reason has such a word. Show it to a person rather than branching on it.

reason.description: The closed token to branch on. Read the device-issues vocabulary for what it means and what to do about it.

severity.description: How loudly to report it. It is fixed by the reason, and it is repeated here so a badge renders before the vocabulary is loaded.

action.description: What a person does about it.

deprecated.description: Present only for an entry on its way out. It names the application release the deprecation shipped in and the entry to move to, when one takes over. The entry keeps being served until a later release removes it.

description.description: The longer description: what raises it, and what it does not mean.

reason.description: The token a device record carries and a client branches on.

severity.description: How loudly to report it. It is fixed by the reason.

summary.description: What is wrong, in one sentence.

affected.description: How many non-retired printers this caller may see carry at least one issue, over every page and whatever filter was applied.

by_severity.description: How many printers carry an issue of each severity, over every page and whatever filter was applied. error, warning and info are always keys, including at zero. A printer carrying issues of two severities counts under both.

counts.description: How many printers carry each reason, keyed by the reason token. Every reason this build knows is a key, including the ones at zero.

severities.description: Every severity an entry may carry, least to most urgent.

version.description: The content version of the set.

vocabulary.description: The vocabulary this set belongs to.

device_id.description: The device the print ran on, as the listing reports it.

device_job_id.description: The job number the machine issued, as the machine spells it. It is not unique: a machine reuses its numbers after a firmware reset and when its counter wraps.

display_name.description: What the machine shows on its screen for the file.

ended.description: When this server saw the print stop. It is absent while the print is running, which is what tells the current job from a finished one.

id.description: The print's identity, a version 7 UUID this server gives each print. A print that reuses a job number the machine issued before is a print of its own with an id of its own.

object_count.description: How many objects of the print the machine reported that can be cancelled one by one, as of the last reading this row holds. It is absent when the machine said nothing about them, and 0 for a print that has none. A finished print keeps the count it ended with.

objects.description: The objects of the print that can be cancelled one by one, ordered by id, as of the last reading this row holds. A finished print keeps the objects it ended with, which says which of them were cancelled. It holds at most 256. When the machine reported more, every cancelled object is kept before the others, so an object missing from the list was not cancelled unless more than 256 were.

outcome.description: How the print ended, as the machine's driver reported it, and what the device.job.settled event says. It is absent while the print is running. A print whose machine said nothing about how it ended reads unknown, and so does one that ended before this server kept the outcome.

path.description: The file on the machine's own storage, as the machine spells it.

progress.description: How far the print had got when this row was last written, in whole percent. A print that finished reads 100 and one that was interrupted keeps the figure it was interrupted at.

started.description: When this server first saw the print.

state.description: The machine's own word for what the print was doing when this row was last written. Read it as an open value: the states belong to the device kind that declares them.

time_remaining_ms.description: How much time the machine thought was left when this row was last written, in milliseconds. The machine reports whole seconds, so this value is always a multiple of 1000.

cursor.description: Opaque text to send back as the cursor parameter for the next page. Empty when this page is the last one. Read nothing out of its form.

items.description: The prints that have ended on this device, newest first. A print that is still running is not here; read the device record for that one.

limit.description: The page size the server applied, which is the cap when a larger one was asked for.

device_job_id.description: The job number the machine issued, as the machine spells it. It is not unique: a machine reuses its numbers after a firmware reset and when its counter wraps.

display_name.description: What the machine shows on its screen for the file, which is not always the last segment of the path.

id.description: The print's identity, a version 7 UUID this server gives each print. It is the same id the jobs route reports. It is empty for a print the machine began since this server last wrote its records, which takes up to two seconds.

object_count.description: How many objects of the print the machine reported that can be cancelled one by one. It is absent when the machine said nothing about them, and 0 for a print that has none.

objects.description: The objects of the print that can be cancelled one by one, ordered by id. It holds at most 256. When the machine reported more, every cancelled object is kept before the others, so an object missing from the list was not cancelled unless more than 256 were.

path.description: The file on the machine's own storage, as the machine spells it. It is empty until the machine has said what it is printing.

progress.description: How far the print has got, in whole percent as the machine reports it.

running.description: Whether the print is still on the bed. It is false once the machine reports a state that ends a job, and a client should read this rather than compare the state itself.

state.description: What the machine says the print is doing, in the machine's own vocabulary. Read it as an open value: the states belong to the device kind that declares them, and the set is published with the kind.

time_remaining_ms.description: How much time the machine thinks is left, in milliseconds. The machine reports whole seconds, so this value is always a multiple of 1000. It is the machine's estimate and not this server's.

current.description: The print on the bed now. It is absent when the machine is not printing.

last.description: The most recent print that has ended. It is absent until one has, and it is not the same row as the current print ever is.

counted.description: Whether the driver behind this printer counts these at all. False means no measurement, not a clean link.

dropped_telemetry.description: Telemetry patches discarded because this server was not reading them fast enough, since this session began.

dropped_telemetry_per_minute.description: The drop rate over the trailing window this reading was measured over.

measured_over_seconds.description: How long the trailing window behind both rates covers. It is reported so that a rate is never read without the span it came from.

refused_frames.description: Frames the printer sent that the driver had no reading of and dropped, since this session began. A frame the driver reads and declines to serve is not counted.

refused_frames_per_minute.description: The refusal rate over the trailing window this reading was measured over. Anything above zero on a connected printer is firmware speaking something this build does not.

directory.description: The directory that was asked for.

fault.description: Why the last read of this path failed. It is held until the next read of the path starts, which refresh=true does. Absent when the last read landed.

items.description: What is directly inside it, in the order the device reported them.

reading.description: True while the printer is reading this path. The rows are what this server held when it answered, none when it held nothing. A read that lands publishes com.prusa.connect.device.files.changed, and the listing it read is then answered without refresh.

reading_since.description: When the read in progress began, as an RFC 3339 string. It is the same for every caller who joins that read. Absent when no read is in progress.

stale.description: True when this server answered from the last listing the printer gave for this path, without asking it again. The printer may hold something else by now: refresh=true has it read the path again.

abbreviation.description: The short name of the material, such as PLA.

package.description: The package the loaded material came in.

artwork.description: Where to fetch a drawing of the machine, present when the driver that reaches it declared one. It is meant for a model a page has no drawing of its own for, and a page that has one keeps its own.

connector.description: The dialect a machine of this model is reached through, by the dialect's bare name. The connectors member of this answer says what that dialect is and what it needs from a person. It is not the driver member of a device record, which names the instance of the dialect one machine actually arrived through.

deprecated.description: Present only for an entry on its way out. It names the application release the deprecation shipped in and the entry to move to, when one takes over. The entry keeps being served until a later release removes it.

device_type_id.description: The code some firmware reports where a model name is expected. A client that meets one resolves it to this row rather than showing the number.

display_name.description: What the machine is sold as. Put it on a card and never parse it.

icon.description: The key to map to a drawing. Models that look alike share one, so a page ships a handful of pictures rather than one per model. Read it as an open value: a newer core may name a key this page has no drawing for, and the answer to that is a generic device.

kind.description: What type of device a machine of this model is. It is printer on every row this build serves, from the same closed set the kind member of a device record is drawn from.

model.description: The machine's own spelling, exactly as a device reports it and exactly as the model member of a device record carries it. It is what the listing's model filter takes.

tool_changer.description: True when the numbered slots of a machine of this model are separate toolheads, as on the Prusa INDX tool changer and the XL, so a page draws a row per tool. It is absent for a model whose slots are feeders on one head, such as an MMU.

connectors.description: The dialects the rows above are reached through, and what each one needs from a person before a machine of that kind can arrive. It rides with the models because the two are read together: a row above names its dialect, and this says what that dialect is.

items.description: One row per model this build can name: the Prusa models a capability profile covers and the models a driver in it declared, ordered by the machine's own spelling. A declared model the server refused has no row; refused lists it.

refused.description: The models a driver in this build declared and the server left out, because the spelling names a Prusa machine or another driver declared it too. A refused model has no row in items. It is empty when every declared model was placed.

version.description: The content version of the set.

vocabulary.description: The vocabulary this set belongs to.

filters.description: How this listing may be narrowed, with the values present in this caller's fleet.

issues.description: What is wrong across every non-retired printer this caller may see, whatever page or filter was asked for.

limit.description: The page size the server applied, which is the cap when a larger one was asked for.

order.description: The direction the server ordered this page in.

sort.description: The field the server ordered this page by.

sorts.description: The fields this listing may be ordered by.

total.description: How many printers the request matched over every page. With with_issues set, it counts only the printers carrying an issue.

keep_both.description: With a storage, send under a free name when the printer holds another file at path, such as usb/part[1].bgcode, keep the printer's file and print the one sent. The answer's path names the file that was started. Refused together with replace.

path.description: The file on the printer, storage-prefixed and relative, such as usb/bracket.bgcode. With a storage it is where the file lands; without one it is the file that is printed.

replace.description: With a storage, delete the file the printer holds at path before sending this one. Without it any file there other than this server's unchanged copy of the same stored file is refused with core.printer/FILE_NAME_TAKEN, so a page can ask the person first.

source.description: The file's path inside that storage, relative to its root. Required with storage and refused without it. A temporary copy is deleted as it is for a send.

storage.description: The storage resource holding the file, by the name it is declared under in the resources block. Absent prints a file the machine already holds.

command.description: What the printer made of the start command. ok false is the machine's refusal and carries fault_code.

path.description: The file that was started, as the printer addresses it.

transfer.description: The transfer as it ended, absent when the file was already on the machine.

reason.description: Why this id stopped naming a machine. ownership_changed is a second registration for the same printer, which is how a machine that changed hands is separated from its previous owner's records. Read it as an open value: a newer core, or a federated peer, may name a reason this build does not carry.

default_order.description: The direction a person reading this field expects first.

field.description: The value the listing's sort parameter takes to order by this field.

accepts.description: Every verb a device in this state accepts, when guarded is true. A verb missing here is one to offer as unavailable in this state. It is a hint: the device's answer to the command decides, and a verb a device's own capability list lacks is one it cannot carry out in any state.

deprecated.description: Present only for an entry on its way out. It names the application release the deprecation shipped in and the entry to move to, when one takes over. The entry keeps being served until a later release removes it.

display_name.description: What to show for a state the client has no words of its own for.

state.description: The value a device record carries and a client branches on.

connector.description: The connector type that declared them, qualified by its namespace.

connectors.description: The connector instances of that type this server runs. A device names its instance under driver, so a client finds the entry for a device by looking its driver up here.

guarded.description: Whether the adapter said which verbs each state accepts. When false, accepts is empty on every state and says nothing.

kind.description: The device kind whose states these are.

namespace.description: The adapter that declared them, derived by the host.

states.description: Every state the kind reports, in the order a person reads them.

transitions.description: Every move between two of those states.

verb.description: The verb that causes the move. Absent when the device makes it alone.

version.description: The content version. This set declares none.

vocabulary.description: The vocabulary this set belongs to.

free_space.description: Bytes left, or null when the printer reported no figure. Zero is a full device.

mountpoint.description: The printer-side path, with its leading slash. It is what identifies the device.

name.description: The first path segment of every file on this storage, such as usb.

read_only.description: Whether the printer refuses writes to this device.

type.description: The device class as the printer spelled it, such as USB. The set is the firmware's, so read it, do not switch on it exhaustively.

items.description: The storage devices, in the order the printer reported them.

reported.description: True once the printer has answered on the connection this server holds now. False means items is the last answer of an earlier connection, or empty because none came yet, and says nothing about the drives in it now.

active.description: Whether the tool is selected, as the architecture's telemetry marks it. A head is active while it is picked, and the one head of a printer that is not a toolchanger always is. A slot is active while it is loaded into its head, even when that head is not picked.

consumed_weight.description: How much of the material loaded in the tool is used, in grams.

features.description: What the nozzle of a head is. A slot prints through the nozzle of the head above it.

feeder.description: The feeder on the tool, such as a multi-material unit. Null is a tool known to have no feeder, and an absent member is a printer that did not say.

heatbreak_fan_rpm.description: The speed of a head's heatbreak fan, in revolutions per minute.

material_package_instance.description: The material loaded in the tool. Null is a tool with nothing loaded, and an absent member is a printer that did not say. A tool with a feeder carries none; its slots do.

nozzle_target_temp.description: The temperature a head is heating to, in degrees Celsius. Null while the heater is off, and absent when the printer did not say.

nozzle_temp.description: The nozzle temperature of a head, in degrees Celsius.

odometer_e.description: How much filament the tool has extruded since its odometers were last reset, in millimetres.

odometer_id.description: A number that changes, without counting up, each time the odometers of the tool are reset. A reset can come at a restart, at the end of a print, at a filament change and at other times. A client that sees it change counts again from zero.

odometer_weight.description: The weight of that filament, in grams. Absent when the printer cannot turn length into weight.

print_fan_rpm.description: The speed of a head's print fan, in revolutions per minute.

type.description: FFF_PRINT_HEAD or FFF_FEEDER_SLOT.

nozzle_hardened.description: Whether the nozzle is hardened against abrasive filament.

nozzle_high_flow.description: Whether the nozzle is a high-flow one.

nozzle_high_temp.description: Whether the nozzle is made for high temperatures.

gcode_tool_map.description: The tool id each G-code tool number Tn selects, when the printer reports it. A G-code tool number it leaves out takes the default: Tn is slot n of the one head when the printer has one head and that head carries a feeder, and head n on any other printer, including one with a feeder on more than one head. Prusa Connect reports it, and the architecture has no such member.

tool_count.description: How many heads the printer has room for, enabled or not. Absent when the printer did not say.

tools.description: Every tool the printer reported, by id. A head is 0, 1 and on, and slot k of the feeder on tool X is X.k. A tool the printer has switched off is null.

bytes_sent.description: How many of the file's bytes this server has put on the wire. A byte the printer asks for again counts once.

bytes_total.description: The file's length as this server measured it before the first byte left.

ended_at.description: When it ended, as an RFC 3339 string. Absent while it runs.

path.description: Where the file lands on the printer, storage-prefixed.

transfer_id.description: The id this server gave the transfer. It is what the stop route and the event stream name it by.

warning.description: What this server could not establish about a transfer that finished, such as a printer that took the file and cannot be asked whether the file is on its storage afterwards. It is a note beside a transfer that succeeded and never a failure, and it is absent for a transfer whose file was confirmed.

keep_both.description: Send under a free name when the printer already holds a file at path, such as usb/part[1].bgcode, and keep the printer's file. The transfer names the path the file lands at. Refused together with replace.

auth_type.description: The type of the principal that authorized the command. Present only for a caller holding view_audit on the device.

authorized_at.description: When the authorization was recorded. Absent for a caller who does not hold view_audit on the device, and for a command that was never authorized.

command_id.description: The invocation's id, minted by this server before the command was authorized. It is the value a caller was handed when it sent the command, and the value every one of the command's durable frames carries.

elapsed_ms.description: How long the invocation took, in milliseconds.

fault_code.description: The registered error code of a failure, absent when the command did not fail with one.

key.description: The caller's idempotency key, absent when none was sent.

machine_reason.description: The device's own word for a refusal, passed through as it spelled it.

ok.description: Whether the device accepted the command. Meaningless when outcome_unknown is set.

origin.description: The device the command was issued against, as kind:id.

outcome_unknown.description: True when this server never observed how the command ended. A command whose caller went away, one whose device lost its connection after the command was sent, and one this server found open after a restart may all have been executed by the machine: the record says it does not know rather than guessing.

requested_at.description: When the instruction was published. Absent for an invocation this server stored an outcome for and never an instruction, which a replay can produce.

settled_at.description: When the outcome was published. Absent while the invocation is open.

status.description: How the invocation ended: succeeded, failed, refused, timed_out, abandoned, unauthorized, or server_restarted. Absent while it is open. It is an open set: a later build may add a word, so show an unknown one rather than refusing the record.

verb.description: The capability key that was invoked.

cursor.description: Opaque text the provider minted, to be sent back as the cursor parameter for the next page. Empty when this page is the last one.

at.description: When the event happened, as the origin's own clock reported it.

epoch.description: The generation of the origin's own store. It changes when that store is recreated, which is what makes sequence unambiguous.

origin.description: What the event came from, as kind:id.

payload.description: The envelope's data member, stored and returned unparsed. Its schema belongs to whoever published the event.

sequence.description: The event's place in its origin's numbering. It is unique inside one epoch and never reused.

type.description: The event type, reverse-DNS and past tense, exactly as it was published.

cursor.description: Opaque text the provider minted, to be sent back as the cursor parameter for the next page. Empty when this page is the last one. Read nothing out of its form.

incomplete.description: Whether the server knows it did not see this window whole. A reader that fell behind loses events, and the window they fell behind in is marked here rather than answered as a quiet hole.

metric.description: The state path the value was reported under, which is the name a series is queried by across firmware versions.

text.description: The reading, for a path that reports a word rather than a number: /state answers IDLE or PRINTING here. Absent where the path reported a number.

value.description: The measurement, for a path that reports a number. Absent where the path reported a word, in which case text carries it.

cursor.description: Opaque text the provider minted, to be sent back as the cursor parameter for the next page. Empty when this page is the last one. Read nothing out of its form.

incomplete.description: Whether the server knows it did not see this window whole.

key.description: The capability key a manifest writes.

summary.description: What the host promises under this key.

name.description: The safe portal account display name.

connectors.description: Every printer dialect this build carries, by qualified name.

routes.description: Every path this origin serves that the OpenAPI document does not publish.

device_code.description: The code the app polls with. It is secret: only the app holds it.

expires_in.description: How many seconds the pairing waits.

interval.description: How many seconds the app waits between two polls.

user_code.description: The code the app shows the person, with a dash in the middle.

verification_uri.description: Where the person confirms the code, on this server's web app.

verification_uri_complete.description: The same page with the code filled in, for a link or a QR code.

cancelled.description: Whether the machine skips the object for the rest of the print.

id.description: The machine's own number for the object. It is the id the core.command.cancel_object and core.command.uncancel_object verbs take.

name.description: The label the machine gives the object, at most 64 bytes. It is absent when the machine reports no names.

limit.description: The page size the server applied, which is the cap when a larger one was asked for.

backup_ready.description: Whether the rollback snapshot completed before live mutation.

bundle_key_id.description: The trusted key that signed an offline bundle manifest.

current_binary.description: The stable path used to start the server.

extension_reviews.description: What each bundled extension asks for and how it differs from the installed one, as preparation found it.

extensions.description: The verified extension archives staged with the core executable.

extensions_approved.description: Whether the operator approved the new asks and older versions the extension reviews name.

external_restore.description: The PostgreSQL databases a rollback left for the operator to restore from their own backup.

failure.description: The terminal or rollback failure reason.

force_printing.description: Whether the operator allowed pausing active prints.

from_version.description: The server version active before this transaction.

metadata.description: The runtime metadata reported by the candidate.

previous_binary.description: The rollback path holding the previous executable.

staged_root.description: The private directory holding every artifact in an offline bundle.

to_version.description: The candidate version selected by this transaction.

updated_at.description: The instant the journal last changed.

verified.description: The signed identity of the candidate executable.

drops.description: How many messages of each kind the link threw away for each reason. A pair that counted nothing is left out.

messages.description: How many messages of each kind ended each way. A pair that counted nothing is left out.

listeners.description: Every network listener this link opened, so an operator sees where other sites reach it.

node_id.description: What this site is called in the network.

nodes.description: Every site below this one, ordered by id.

public_key.description: This site's public identity key as text. The private half is on no path that reaches this value.

running.description: Whether the link is serving right now. Everything below is absent while it is not.

type.description: The registered implementation this link is built from.

uplink.description: The site above this one, and absent on a site that names none.

address.description: The interface it is bound to.

port.description: The port it accepts on. Absent for a transport with no port.

protocol.description: What the listener speaks, as the link names it.

items.description: Every link the caller may see, ordered by name.

count.description: How many messages of that kind ended that way since the link started.

kind.description: The link protocol's name for the type of message.

outcome.description: The link protocol's name for what the link did with it: handled, passed on, or thrown away.

address.description: Where the connection to this node goes.

admission.description: Whether the node may act here. A node stays pending under explicit enrolment until an operator approves it, and a node an operator revoked stays in the list as revoked.

alive.description: Whether the connection to the node is open right now.

id.description: The node's identity in the network.

last_heartbeat.description: When something last arrived from the node. Absent until something has.

latency_ms.description: The last round trip the link measured, in milliseconds. Absent on a protocol that measures none.

path.description: Where the node sits in the tree. Absent before it joins.

public_key.description: The node's public identity key as text.

role.description: What this node is to the one reporting it.

code.description: The protocol's number for a refusal. Absent unless the state is denied.

connected_at.description: When the connection last opened. Absent until one has, and it stays at the last opening while the state is lost.

fault_code.description: The link's own registered error code for a refusal, written as domain/REASON. reason.description: The other end's own sentence for the state, for a person to read. Absent when it gave none.

retryable.description: Whether the same request may succeed if sent again.

password.description: Their password. It is never logged or echoed.

username.description: The name this person logs in with.

expires_at.description: When this server stops accepting the credential.

at.description: When the host read the memory.

value.description: The memory the process used, in bytes. Absent when the host could not read it, which is not zero.

name.description: The stable migration name.

version.description: The migration version number.

dsn.description: With mode postgres, the postgres:// URL of the module's database, with the role and the password the module logs in with. It is stored in this server's own configuration and never answered by a read. Refused with any other mode.

instance.description: The instance that was granted the database, as kind:name. Installing the same module under this name again takes the database back.

left_at.description: When the grant was given up.

provisioned.description: Whether this server made the database and its role on its own Postgres server.

purge.description: What a purge does to it. drop drops the database and the role this server made. delete deletes the SQLite file. forget forgets the record and leaves a database the operator named alone, because it is theirs.

type.description: The module's type. Only a module of this type takes the database back.

where.description: Where the database is: the path of the SQLite file, or host:port/name for Postgres. The role and its password are never answered.

why.description: removed when the module was removed. moved when an update put the module's database somewhere else. not_granted when an update granted no database, because it was installed without approve or the release asks for none.

done.description: dropped, deleted or forgotten. A forgotten database is still where it was.

instance.description: The instance that was granted the database, as kind:name.

where.description: Where the database was, as list-module-databases names it.

items.description: Every database a module left behind that this caller administers, oldest first. Empty when there is none.

enabled.description: Whether that module is switched on. While one that is requires this module, this module cannot be switched off.

module.description: Its namespace.

version.description: The range of this module's releases it requires.

from.description: Where the connection starts: the module's process on the server, or its page in the person's browser.

host.description: The host it connects to: an exact name, *.domain one level deep, or an IP address. Absent when option names the host.

option.description: The setting of the module whose value the operator sets to the host. Absent when host names it.

sends.description: What leaves the server or the browser on that connection, in the author's words.

why.description: Why the module connects there, in the author's words.

module.description: The namespace of the module the plan installs.

types.description: The file types both claim, such as .3mf.

use.description: What both do with the files: file_analysis reads them for the server, file_view draws what they hold.

with.description: The namespace of the enabled module it conflicts with.

module.description: The installed module identifier.

needed_to_start.description: Whether the server needs this module serving to start.

outcome.description: The predicted module outcome after the update.

reason.description: The compatibility reason for this outcome.

items.description: The modules this deployment can install: the local index in the order it lists them, then the marketplace's rows for modules the local index does not name. Empty when the operator has pointed this server at neither.

marketplace.description: The marketplace the rows were read from, and whether it answered. Absent when core.marketplace.url is empty.

added.description: On an update made with approve, what this release asks for that the release it replaced did not, and that was granted, in the words requests uses. A permission or an event the operator took away from the module stays away, and a records room the operator set is kept. Empty for a new install.

approved.description: What an install made with approve gave the module, one per line in the words requests uses: each permission a grant was written for, check_absent_people when the module may ask about a person it is not serving, list_people when it may list the people this server holds, the room granted its records as records <n> MiB, each event, the data directory, the database of its own, and each port granted with approve_listen. Empty without approve.

database_left.description: On an update that moved the module's own database, or granted none, where the old database is, without its credential. It is kept with its data and listed by list-module-databases until purge-module-database deletes it.

dependencies.description: The modules this install added because the release requires them, as module@version, in the order they were written.

enabled.description: Whether the instance was switched on. Without approve it is false, and put-resource switches it on once the requests below have been read.

instance.description: The declared instance, as kind:name. It is what the resources listing and every grant name it by.

kind.description: The resource kind it is declared under, as the manifest names it.

migrations.description: The migrations this start applied to the module's own database, in order, by the name the module's ledger records. They ran in one transaction. Empty when there was nothing to apply.

namespace.description: The namespace its routes, its bundle and its records are served under.

reason.description: Why the module did not start, when state is failed or retrying. It is the message list-resources carries on the instance's failed condition, such as a required setting nobody wrote or settings the module refused. A settings change written with put-resource starts the instance again.

requests.description: What the manifest asks for and has not been given: a permission, more room for its records, an event, a data directory, a database of its own or a port, one per line. Empty for an install made with approve, except a port, which stays here until an install is made with approve_listen. Read them, then install again with approve.

restart.description: Whether this server has to be restarted before the module takes effect. It is false for an install this server reconciled, which is every install it accepts while it is serving. When it is true the declaration is written and the next start reads it.

root.description: Where the files landed on this server.

running.description: Whether the module is serving now. It is true only when state is ready or degraded. An install made without approve leaves the instance switched off, so it is false until put-resource switches it on.

runtime.description: How the type is reached: service for a module that runs a process, asset for one that is only a bundle.

schema_version.description: For a module with a database of its own that is running, the schema version its database holds after this start migrated it. Absent for a module that is not running or reports none.

state.description: The state the module reached, in the words list-resources uses. The install waits a few seconds for the start to finish. ready and degraded are serving. failed and retrying did not start, and reason says why. starting is a start still in progress when the wait ended: read list-resources for the rest. pending is an instance waiting for something it requires, or for the restart that restart asks for. disabled is an install made without approve.

type.description: The registered type the declaration names, which is the namespace and the manifest's name joined.

verified.description: How many files were checked against the release's checksum file. Zero is a release that carries none.

version.description: The version the manifest declares.

withheld.description: What an install made with approve could not give the module: each permission no grant was written for, one per line. Write that grant on a printer by hand, or leave the module without it. Empty without approve.

name.description: The name the manifest gives the port. An install moves a port by this name.

network.description: The transport the port is on.

port.description: The port the manifest asks for.

why.description: The sentence the manifest gives for the port, for the person who approves it.

browse_url.description: Where a person browses its Connect modules in a browser.

community.description: Whether an organization administrator chose to list the community extensions, the rows whose trust is verified or community. enabled.description: Whether this server reads it. False when a person switched it off, and then the index lists none of its rows and nothing is fetched from it.

problem.description: Why the last read failed, in this server's words. A stale copy of the catalogue may still be listed.

reachable.description: Whether the marketplace answered the last read. False when it has not answered yet or the last refresh failed; the local rows are still listed, and so is a stale copy.

read_at.description: When the catalogue the rows come from was read, in RFC 3339. Absent when it has never been read.

stale.description: Whether the marketplace rows are a copy kept after the last read failed. reachable is then false and problem says why.

committed_bytes.description: The sum of the memory budgets of the enabled service modules.

pool_bytes.description: The memory the budgets of the enabled service modules are meant to fit in together. Absent when the server cannot learn it: the operator set none and the machine's memory could not be read.

source.description: Who set the pool: configured is core.modules_memory, detected is the machine's memory less a reserve for the server and the system. Absent when the server cannot learn the pool.

allowed_origins.description: The browser origins the release's manifest asks this server to answer, each an exact https origin. An install with approve lets a page served from one call the API from a browser while the module is switched on.

calls.description: The namespaces of the other modules whose routes the release's manifest asks to call.

database.description: Whether the release's manifest asks for a database of its own.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the release archive, which an install from this row is checked against.

source.description: Where that release's bytes are, which an install passes back as from.

staged_routes.description: The routes whose request body the release's manifest asks the server to write into its data directory, each with the largest body it asks for.

suggests.description: The modules the release works better with, each with the reason. A suggestion installs nothing.

title.description: The name a person reads, where the row has one beside the manifest's short name.

trust.description: How far the marketplace vouches for the module: community, verified or official.

version.description: The release the index offers.

view_types.description: The file types the release's file-view entries draw for, and * for an entry that draws for every file.

by.description: The namespace of the module that says it, or the operator.

constraint.description: The constraint it puts, when the reason is one.

text.description: The reason, as an operator reads it.

items.description: The reasons, empty when there is none.

approve.description: Whether to write the permissions and the events the manifest asks for and switch the instance on. Without it the module is installed, switched off, and the answer says what it asked for.

approve_listen.description: With approve, also grant the ports the manifest lists under needs.listen. A port is reachable from the network, so it is approved apart from the other requests. Without it the module is installed without its ports, and requests lists each one.

database.description: With approve, where the database of its own goes, for a manifest that asks for one under needs.database. Omitted on a first install, it is a SQLite file in the module's data directory. Omitted on an update, the database the module already has is kept. Refused without approve, and for a manifest that asks for no database.

dependencies.description: The modules plan-module-install answered for this release, which the person approved with it. The install adds exactly these, in the order the plan gives, with the same approve. A plan that resolves differently now is refused with MODULE_PLAN_CHANGED and nothing is written. Omitted, the install adds nothing and is refused with MODULE_PLAN_CHANGED when the release requires a module this server does not have.

expect.description: With approve, the requests the page showed the operator before they approved, usually copied from the index row. An install whose manifest asks for anything beyond them is refused with MODULE_REQUESTS_CHANGED and nothing is written. Omitted, only a marketplace install is held, to what the marketplace lists for the release.

from.description: Where the bytes are: an https URL of the release archive, which takes sha256, or a directory or .tar.gz on this server's own filesystem. Omitted, the release is the one the configured marketplace offers for this module and version, fetched from where it says and checked against its digest. Fetching a release from a repository by tag is not in this build.

listen.description: With approve_listen, the port to grant under each name the manifest lists, in place of the port it asks for. The network stays the one the manifest names. A name the manifest does not list is refused.

memory_mib.description: With approve, the memory budget of the module's process in MiB, from 16 to 8192, in place of what its manifest recommends. Zero follows the recommendation, or on an update keeps a budget the operator set, and without approve a value is refused.

module.description: The module's path, which is the repository it is built from. The namespace every address of this module is built from is derived from it.

records_mib.description: With approve, the room to grant the module's records in MiB, in place of what its manifest asks for. Zero grants what it asks for, or on an update keeps a room the operator set, and without approve a value is refused.

settings.description: The module's settings, written into the same declaration: the keys the manifest declares under options, such as the address of the system it sends to. A key left out takes the manifest's default. A required key with no value stops the start, and the answer's state is failed with the key in reason. On a reinstall of the same module, leaving settings out keeps each stored key the new manifest still declares with the same type, and a credential sent as the marker a read answers keeps the stored credential, as put-resource does. A release under another module path is refused with MODULE_NAME_TAKEN. It is what module add -settings reads from a file.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the .tar.gz, as 64 hex digits. Required when from is a URL: a fetched release whose bytes hash to anything else is refused before it is unpacked. Ignored for a path on this server, whose checksums.txt is verified instead.

version.description: The release to accept, in the range grammar a module author already writes: 1.2.3 names one release, ^1.2.0 names a set, * takes whatever the manifest says. The manifest is held to it.

approve_listen.description: With approve, also grant the ports this module lists under needs.listen. Without it the module is installed without its ports.

expect.description: With approve, the requests the plan showed for this module. Its manifest is held to them. An approved install whose plan carries a module without them is refused with MODULE_REQUESTS_CHANGED and nothing is written.

module.description: The module's path.

sha256.description: The digest the plan answered for this release. The install is refused with MODULE_PLAN_CHANGED when the release it would fetch now has another digest. Omitted only for a release the plan answered without one.

version.description: The release.

required_by.description: The installed modules that require this one. While any is listed, the removal is refused with MODULE_REQUIRED_BY.

unused.description: The modules an install added for this one that nothing else requires once it is gone. uninstall-module removes them with with_unused, and leaves them installed without it.

name.description: The name of the header.

reason.description: Why the module reads it, as its manifest says.
examples: PrusaSlicer 2 says whether to print the file it uploads

required.description: Whether the module cannot work without the header. An install that would not grant it is refused, and the instance does not start without it.

allowed_origins.description: The browser origins the module asks this server to answer, each an exact https origin. A page served from one may call the API from a browser while the module is switched on.

calls.description: The namespaces of the other modules whose routes the module calls.

check_absent_people.description: Whether the module may ask about a person it is not serving.

checks.description: The actions the module asks about for a person it serves, without taking them as itself.

data.description: Whether the module asks for a writable directory of its own.

database.description: Whether the module asks for a database of its own. The operator chooses where it goes with database on the install.

events.description: Each endpoint the module publishes on, against the event name after its namespace.

list_people.description: Whether the module may list the people this server holds, with their names.

listen.description: The ports the module listens on for a protocol of its own. They are approved with approve_listen.

memory_mib.description: The memory budget the module recommends for its process, in MiB. Zero is no recommendation, and the server default of 128 MiB applies.

permissions.description: The actions the module takes as itself.

public_routes.description: The routes the module answers without a signed-in caller, each a method and a path under its mount, such as POST /hooks/announce/.

records_mib.description: The room the module asks for its records, in MiB. Zero is the default room.

request_headers.description: The request headers the server passes to the module's routes beside the ones every module gets, each with the reason the module gives.

staged_routes.description: The routes whose request body the server writes into the module's data directory, each with the largest body the module asks for.

max_mib.description: The largest request body on the route, in MiB. A larger body is refused with BODY_TOO_LARGE.

method.description: The HTTP method of the route.

path.description: The path of the route under the module's mount, where a segment written {name} matches any one segment.

title.description: What the module says the route takes, in words, such as Upload from PrusaSlicer 2.6 and later. Only what a module asks carries it.

key.description: The key the record is stored under.

module.description: Its namespace.

title.description: The name a person reads, from its manifest.

version.description: Its release.

from.description: The entry to move, relative to the storage root.

to.description: Where it should be, relative to the same storage root.

items.description: Every printer this server hears, sorted by name. The list never holds more than 256.

address.description: The address the other printer's API answers on.

device_id.description: The id of the printer on this server that connects from this address, or last connected from it and is away now. It is absent for a printer that has not connected here since this server started, and for one the caller may not observe.

name.description: The name the other printer announces, which is its title.

port.description: The port of the other printer's API.

services.description: The mDNS service names it answers under, sorted.

tls.description: True when that port expects https.

url.description: The address of the other printer's own web page.

cookie.description: The cookie Set-Cookie sets, for an app that stores it into its web view itself.

expires_at.description: When the page session ends. It is at most an hour away, and never after the app's credential expires.

expires.description: When the cookie and the page session end.

http_only.description: Always true: no script on the page may read the cookie.

name.description: The cookie's name, the session cookie of this server.

path.description: The cookie's path.

secure.description: True unless this server is reached over plain HTTP.

value.description: The page session. Store it only in the cookie, never where a page script reads it.

label.description: A note the administrator wrote for the listing.

label.description: A note for the listing: whose account this is.

provider.description: The identity provider type that vouches for the subject, as its plugin registers it.

subject.description: The subject as the token's sub claim spells it.

current_password.description: Required to change your own password. An administrator resetting another account sends none.

new_password.description: At least 8 bytes and at most 72.

name.description: The stable logical database name.

path.description: The dump path relative to the backup directory.

sha256.description: The lowercase SHA-256 digest of the dump.

disk_available.description: The free bytes available in the update filesystem.

disk_required.description: The estimated free bytes required for update and rollback.

managed.description: Whether this process may replace its executable.

module_impacts.description: The predicted compatibility effect on installed modules.

printing.description: The identifiers of devices with active work.

writable.description: Whether the executable directory passed its write probe.

display_name.description: The signed-in person's display name: a local account's, or the name the identity provider last sent.

email.description: The address the identity provider last sent for the signed-in person. Absent for a local account.

principal.description: The subject the authorization graph is keyed by for this caller.

username.description: The signed-in person's login name. Present only when the subject is a local user account that still exists.

width_mm.description: The width of the bed, in millimetres.

max_y_mm.description: The back edge, in millimetres from the bed's origin.

min_x_mm.description: The left edge, in millimetres from the bed's origin.

min_y_mm.description: The front edge, in millimetres from the bed's origin.

features.description: The firmware features M862.6 lines name, such as Input shaper and MMU3.

bed.description: The printable volume of the printer profile the file was sliced with. Absent when the file does not say.

bounds.description: The area the objects cover on the bed. Absent when the file does not say.

checks.description: What the start of the G-code asks the printer to verify before it prints. Absent when the G-code could not be read, and an empty object when it was read and asks for nothing.

estimated_seconds.description: The print time the slicer estimated for its normal mode, in whole seconds.

filament_g.description: How much filament the print uses, in grams.

filament_mm.description: How much filament the print uses, in millimetres.

filament_profile.description: The slicer's filament profile the file was sliced with. A multi-tool file reports the first.

filaments.description: What the print needs of each filament, by the T number that selects it, T0 first. A file sliced for one filament has one entry. The single values above are the first filament's. Which tool of a printer a filament lands on is the printer's tool tree's to say.

high_flow.description: The file was sliced for a high flow nozzle. A multi-tool file reports the first tool.

layer_height_mm.description: The layer height the file was sliced at, in millimetres.

max_layer_z_mm.description: The height of the top layer, in millimetres.

nozzle_mm.description: The nozzle diameter the file was sliced for, in millimetres. A multi-tool file reports the first.

objects.description: The objects the slicer labelled, in the order of its objects_info, with the outline of each on the bed. A printer cancels an object by its id. Absent when the file labels none.

print_profile.description: The slicer's print profile the file was sliced with, such as 0.20mm STRUCTURAL @MK4IS 0.4.

printer_model.description: The printer the file was sliced for, such as MK4IS.

printer_profile.description: The slicer's printer profile the file was sliced with.

thumbnail_height.description: The height in pixels of the picture the thumbnail path serves for this file. Absent when the file carries no picture.

thumbnail_width.description: The width in pixels of the picture the thumbnail path serves for this file. Absent when the file carries no picture.

abrasive.description: Whether the filament wears a nozzle that is not hardened.

bed_temp_c.description: The bed temperature the filament asks for, in degrees Celsius.

colour.description: The colour the slicer shows the filament in, as #RRGGBB.

filament_g.description: How much of this filament the print uses, in grams.

filament_mm.description: How much of this filament the print uses, in millimetres.

first_layer_bed_temp_c.description: The bed temperature of the first layer, in degrees Celsius.

first_layer_nozzle_temp_c.description: The nozzle temperature of the first layer, in degrees Celsius.

high_flow.description: Whether the filament was sliced for a high-flow nozzle.

material.description: The filament type, such as PLA.

nozzle_mm.description: The nozzle diameter the filament was sliced for, in millimetres.

nozzle_temp_c.description: The nozzle temperature, in degrees Celsius.

used.description: Whether the print extrudes this filament: more than 0.0003 g, the firmware's own threshold. Absent when the file does not say how much of each filament it uses.

diameter_mm.description: The nozzle diameter the line asks for, in millimetres.

hardened.description: Whether the line asks for a hardened nozzle. Absent when the line does not say.

high_flow.description: Whether the line asks for a high-flow nozzle. Absent when the line does not say.

index.description: n of the Tn the line names, counted from 0. A line that names no T is about T0.

id.description: The object's number in objects_info, which M486 S and a printer's cancel list use.

name.description: The label the slicer gave the object, such as Cube (Instance 2). It is not unique.

outline.description: The object's outline on the bed it was sliced on, in millimetres from the bed's origin.

x.description: Millimetres from the bed's origin along its width.

y.description: Millimetres from the bed's origin along its depth.

args.description: Argument values as text, checked against the capability descriptor before sending.

key.description: The caller's idempotency key, scoped to this printer. While a command sent under this key is still running, a second request carrying it is not sent to the printer again: it is answered with the first one's command_id and duplicate true. An empty key is not deduplicated. It is not remembered across a restart of this server, and it is not a queue: a command that must survive an outage is desired state, reconciled when the printer reconnects.

verb.description: The capability key to invoke. It must be one the printer's capability set lists.

completed.description: How many lines the printer accepted, counting from the first.

steps.description: One entry per line submitted, in the order they were sent.

stopped.description: Whether the run stopped before the end. Nothing is undone: the lines that ran, ran.

force.description: Run each command out of band, ahead of the print queue.

lines.description: The commands, in order, one gcode command each.

answer.description: What the printer said back to this line, in its own words. Shipping Buddy firmware answers nothing, so it is empty on a real machine; the simulator answers the way a serial port would, so M105 comes back as the temperatures and M114 as the position. It is the machine's vocabulary rather than this API's, so show it to a person and branch on code instead.

code.description: The error code for a line this server refused, as the error reference names it. A line the printer refused carries none.

detail.description: What went wrong with a refused line, in this API's words.

gcode.description: The line, as it was sent.

machine_reason.description: Why the printer refused this line, in the printer's own words, passed through as it spelled them. It is the machine's vocabulary rather than this API's: no list of values is published, a firmware may send one this server has never seen, and it is meant to be shown to a person rather than branched on. Absent on a line the printer accepted, on a line this server refused, and for a printer whose dialect has no such word. To branch on a failure, read code instead.

status.description: accepted, refused, or not_attempted for a line after the one that stopped the run.

answer.description: What the printer said back, in its own words, and absent for a printer that answers a command without saying anything. Shipping Buddy firmware answers nothing, so this is empty on a real machine and carries the serial reply on the simulator: ok for most lines, the temperatures for M105, the position for M114. It is the machine's vocabulary rather than this API's, so show it to a person and branch on fault_code instead.

command_id.description: This invocation's id, minted by the server. The lifecycle events of the command carry it, so it is what a caller reads its record back under.

duplicate.description: True when a command under this idempotency key was already running for this printer. The printer was not sent the command a second time, and command_id names the invocation that is running.

fault_code.description: The registered code of the refusal, absent on a command the printer accepted. It is this API's vocabulary rather than the machine's, so it is what a client branches on: read it with the error reference, which publishes each code's retry hint. core.printer/COMMAND_REFUSED is a refusal the printer gave a reason for, carried in machine_reason; core.printer/COMMAND_REFUSED_WITHOUT_REASON is one it gave no word for at all, and carries no machine reason.

machine_reason.description: Why the printer refused, in the printer's own words, passed through as it spelled them. It is the machine's vocabulary rather than this API's: no list of values is published, a firmware may send one this server has never seen, and it is meant to be shown to a person rather than branched on. Absent on a command the printer accepted, and absent for a printer whose dialect has no such word: a printer that refused and said nothing carries fault_code and no reason. To branch on the refusal, read fault_code beside it.

ok.description: Whether the printer accepted the command.

substituted.description: Parameters the printer replaced, and with what.

code.description: The stable identifier for this failure, as domain/REASON. A client branches on it and indexes its message bundle by it. Codes in the core namespace are documented in the error reference; a code from any other domain belongs to an extension.

detail.description: The sentence for this occurrence. Absent when there is none, or when the code is registered as redacted.

instance.description: The request path this occurrence was answered on.

params.description: The values the code interpolates, keyed by the names the error reference publishes for it. Each value is a JSON scalar. Absent when the code is registered as redacted.

retryable.description: Whether the same request may succeed if sent again.

status.description: The HTTP status the response was sent with.

title.description: The registered summary of the code, the same for every occurrence.

trace_id.description: The W3C trace id of the request, which an operator finds in the log.

type.description: The RFC 9457 type URI: the error reference page and this code's own section of it, so opening it lands on what the code means and what to do about it. A page can offer it as a help link. Nothing has to dereference it, and an air-gapped install loses nothing by not doing so.

path.description: The directory path relative to its protected root.

directories.description: The directories originally present below a protected directory.

kind.description: The original path kind: file, directory or missing.

name.description: The stable logical name of the protected path.

resolved.description: The canonical protected path used to detect changed parent links.

source.description: The original absolute path of the protected path.

items.description: What the purge did to each database left behind under the instance.

required.description: Whether this instance failing makes the process unready.

serving.description: Whether calls are being routed to it.

state.description: The lifecycle state the supervision plane last observed.

app.description: Where the web app stands: served, off when core.frontend.enabled is false, or absent when this build carries none. It never makes the process unready: a deployment serving its own page wants this off.

blocked.description: The required instances that are not serving, in the configuration's order. Empty when ready, and empty for a caller this server could not identify.

declared.description: How many instances the merged configuration declares.

discovery.description: Where the local network announcement stands: announcing, hidden when a person hid this server, off when core.discovery.enabled is false, or failed when this machine would not open the mDNS socket or other machines hold every name it may take. Absent for a caller who does not hold view_resource on the link resource kind, the grant GET /api/v1/discovery/visibility takes. It never makes the process unready: an instance nobody can discover still serves every request.

instances.description: The declared instances this caller may see, and where each is. Empty for a caller this server could not identify.

ready.description: False while an instance the configuration declares required is not serving.

serving.description: How many declared instances calls are being routed to.

collides_with.description: What already answers to the spelling: a Prusa model, the device type code of one, or the other drivers that declared it.

connector.description: The bare name of the dialect that declared it, as the connector member of a model row names a dialect.

qualified.description: The namespace-qualified name of the dialect that declared it, as the qualified member of a connectors entry carries it. It tells apart two modules registering one bare name.

remedy.description: What the person who composed the build does about the refusal.

approved.description: Whether anything has let this device through: an operator, or a connector configured to approve on arrival. The listing carries only registrations waiting for a decision, so it is false on every row there.

code.description: What the device is polling with, and what an operator reads off its screen. It is the id every operation on this surface takes.

connector.description: The connector instance holding this registration. A deployment with several connectors reads it to know which wire the device is on.

device_id.description: The device this approval bound the machine to, which is the id every device operation takes. It is on the answer to an approval, so a page that just let a machine through opens its device page without matching serial numbers against the fleet. It is absent on a row waiting for a decision, because no device exists until somebody decides, and absent on an approval that bound none: a registration carrying no fingerprint has nothing to bind an id to, and such a machine is given one at its first handshake instead.

fingerprint.description: The identity the device keeps across reconnections. Once the registration is approved, this is what the connector's allowlist is keyed by.

firmware.description: The firmware version the device reported, in its own spelling.

model.description: The model the device reported, in its own spelling.

serial.description: The serial number the device reported, in its own spelling.

checked_at.description: The instant the migration rehearsal completed.

duration_ms.description: The rehearsal wall time in milliseconds.

binary.description: The executable asset compatible with this server.

name.description: The human-readable release name.

notes.description: The release notes published with this version.

prerelease.description: Whether this release belongs to a prerelease channel.

published_at.description: The instant GitHub published the release.

version.description: The semantic release version.

destructive.description: Whether the item is drawn as one that deletes or stops something.

devices.description: On a device slot, the devices the entry is drawn for. Absent for every device.

file_types.description: For a slot handed a file, the file types the entry is drawn for: a lowercase extension with its dot, such as .3mf. Absent for every file.

icon.description: The icon the item draws, and absent for none.

id.description: The action's name within its list, one DNS label.

message.description: The human sentence, when there is one.

observed_generation.description: The instance generation this condition was written from.

reason.description: A CamelCase token a program branches on. Always present.

status.description: Whether the axis holds: True, False, or Unknown when nothing has observed it yet.

camera_section.description: A section under each camera in a printer's Cameras tab. A module draws nothing for a camera it does not know.

cards.description: A card a person places on a dashboard, sized on its grid and drawn with the settings the person chose.

device_action.description: An item in the action menu at the top of a printer's page. The module runs it with the printer's id.

schema.description: The schema the database holds, as the running module reported it after it migrated the database at its last start. Absent while the module is not running, and for a module that reports none.

server.description: For postgres, the server's host and port and the database name, as host:port/name. The role and its password are never answered.

applied.description: The migrations the module applied at its last start, in order, by the name its ledger records. Empty when the database was already up to date.

compat.description: The compat floor the database records: a release whose highest schema version is below it refuses the database.

version.description: The highest schema version the database holds.

resident.description: True: the entry is drawn only on a device whose record has resident: true, which is a printer this server runs on. Absent when the selector names no such condition. A client draws no entry whose selector carries a key or a value it cannot read.

config.description: Settings owned and validated by the implementation named by type.

enabled.description: Whether the supervisor starts this instance.

generation.description: Counts accepted changes to the declaration.

hidden_contributions.description: UI contributions of a module hidden for every viewer, each as slot key and identity joined by one /: pages/<path>, or device_card, device_section, device_tab, device_action, file_action or print_section followed by /<id>. Omitted or empty hides nothing.

kind.description: The resource kind: what the instance plugs into.

memory_mib.description: The memory budget of a service module's process, in MiB, from 16 to 8192. module.description: For a module, what its manifest said about itself: the release, one line about it, and who answers for it. Absent otherwise.

mount.description: For a module the operator mounted at a root prefix such as /graphql, that prefix: its routes are served there instead of under /api/v1/modules/{namespace}/. Absent otherwise.

name.description: The operator-chosen name, unique within the kind.

namespace.description: For a module, the namespace its routes are served under at /api/v1/modules/{namespace}/, and for an asset module the namespace its files are served under at /api/v1/modules/{namespace}/ui/. Absent otherwise.

on_over_memory.description: What the host does when a service module's process goes over its memory budget: stop kills the process and counts towards switching the module off, warn keeps it running and marks the status over_budget. openapi_url.description: For a running module that ships an OpenAPI document, the path it is served at. Absent otherwise.

required.description: Whether the process refuses to serve while this instance is not ready.

runtime.description: How the type is reached: compiled into this binary, launched as a child process, a script the host runs, or a directory of files the host verifies and serves.

source.description: Which input declared this instance. Only overlay is writable through the API.

staged_routes.description: For a service module, each route whose request body the server writes into the module's data directory, with the largest body it takes, from 1 to 4096 MiB.
